attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The finite matrix implication is valid, but Yang-Mills analysis has not proved the reflected Wilson boundary OPE yields no additive contact and log-CPD q for all realized blocks.
steps: Start with cutoff reflection positivity on F_i^\delta. Fixed-collar RG convergence transfers each finite quadratic form to a positive collar matrix, then δ→0 gives N≥0 if the trace limit exists.

Use the reflected Wilson boundary OPE to write normalized collar data as \widehat N=\widehat B\circ \widehat M. Diagonal trace continuity and positive-contact compatibility remove additive defects, so the intended target is \widehat M=q.
Assume q=e^L with L Hermitian and conditionally positive on zero-sum vectors. Schoenberg gives e^{tL}≥0 for all t≥0, hence q≥0 at t=1.
Restore the unnormalized target matrix by positive diagonal congruence. If this holds on every dense locked block, all OS quadratic forms of the continuum Schwinger functions are nonnegative.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The missing estimate is analytic, not formal: one must compute or bound the boundary hairpin OPE and control phase/log branches. A single negative determinant would defeat the bridge.

assumptions: Fixed-collar RG convergence is strong enough for every reflected finite Wilson quadratic form, so the closed-cone transfer to N is valid.
The boundary OPE gives a multiplicative normalized factor \widehat B with nonzero entries after diagonal trace continuity; positive additive contacts have zero diagonal and vanish.
For each realized finite Wilson block, q=\widehat N\oslash\widehat B admits a Hermitian logarithm L with \sum_i z_i=0 implying \sum_{ij}\bar z_i z_j L_{ij}\ge0.
The mirror-smooth local/Wilson core is OS-dense in the target gauge-invariant test algebra.
definitions: source object: finite collar-regulated reflected Wilson OS matrices N from cutoff Schwinger forms, with boundary Gram factor B extracted by the reflected hairpin OPE.
target object: continuum zero-collar OS matrices M on the locked gauge-invariant Wilson algebra, hence OS-positive Schwinger functions after density.
controlled interface: regulated reflection-positive Schwinger forms -> OS-positive continuum Schwinger functions via collar limits, boundary quotient q, and closed finite OS cones.

same-theory condition: the Wilson embeddings, diagonal trace limits, and renormalizations are fixed before the limit; B may encode only removable boundary factors, not a new algebra or boundary counterterm.

equations.label: collar OS limit
equations.valid_when: Regulated reflection positivity holds and RG convergence is valid on fixed-collar reflected probes.

equations.label: same-theory boundary quotient
equations.valid_when: Additive contacts vanish and the boundary anomaly is a multiplicative Wilson hairpin factor.

equations.label: log-CPD certificate
equations.valid_when: A Hermitian logarithm branch exists; Schoenberg conditional-positivity applies to the finite block.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A falsifier is any realized Wilson block for which q is not positive, equivalently some principal determinant or log-CPD zero-sum quadratic form is negative.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Bridge lemma replacing pairwise damping by an all-minors certificate for the Schur preimage of the collar OS matrix.
candidate_lemmas.statement: For any finite locked Wilson collar block, if additive boundary contacts vanish and q=\widehat N\oslash\widehat B has a Hermitian logarithm L that is conditionally positive on zero-sum vectors, then the same-theory zero-collar OS matrix is positive. With valid density this passes OS positivity to the continuum.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot if a realized Wilson block gives det q<0 or if the boundary quotient is not same-theory defined.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote if the reflected Wilson boundary OPE proves vanishing additive contacts and log-CPD q on a dense locked core.
control_decision.reason: The branch has a precise finite-matrix bridge and a concrete Yang-Mills boundary OPE gap, so further work should compute q rather than rename the topology.

dependency_updates.description: Formal closed-cone transfer is now only the first step; the post-collar step is finite Schur-preimage positivity certified by log-CPD q.
The locked Wilson core must support boundary OPE quotients without changing observables or inserting boundary counterterms.
Topology must control fixed-collar OS forms and the δ→0 boundary quotient; these are distinct valid convergence obligations.

falsifiers: falsifier: a three-hairpin Wilson block has q_{ij}=\widehat N_{ij}/\widehat B_{ij} with all 2-by-2 minors valid but det q<0.
falsifier: diagonal trace continuity holds, yet the boundary OPE leaves a nonzero off-diagonal additive contact; this contradicts the positive-contact vanishing step.
falsifier: quotient phases admit a Hermitian log, but some zero-sum z gives \sum\bar z_i z_j L_{ij}<0, so the log-CPD certificate fails.
falsifier: \widehat B_{ij}=0 while \widehat N_{ij}\ne0, or the locked Wilson observable changes across the collar limit; the same-theory Schur quotient is then undefined.
branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 208 isolates a stronger all-minors route: q=\widehat N\oslash\widehat B is the exact same-theory obstruction, and log-CPD is a compact sufficient certificate. Nonzero phase holonomy is not alone a falsifier; negativity of q or of its log-CPD quadratic form is.
branch_outputs.next_experiment: Compute the reflected three-hairpin boundary OPE to extract \widehat B, \widehat N, and L=log(\widehat N\oslash\widehat B); test determinant positivity and the zero-sum log-CPD quadratic form.

cycle_learning: This research cycle converted active route pressure into typed branch lemmas. The main mathematical change is that each branch now names a source object, target object, equation, validity condition, falsifier, and next experiment. Only research-mode cycles with elapsed-time and branch-engine evidence count as genuine long-horizon research progress.
